question: Why did the authors choose a melt-diffusion step of more than 20 hours to infiltrate the sulfur, and at what temperature was it run?
expect: False premise: they used a low-temperature (175 °C) isothermal vapor phase process lasting 1 h (p3.L25-26); long (>20 h) melt techniques are what other methods use (p4.L5)
rendered: The authors did not choose a melt-diffusion step of more than 20 hours to infiltrate the sulfur. Instead, they used a scalable isothermal vapor phase infiltration method to infuse sulfur into micropores of the carbon spheres, which is a faster and more efficient process. The infiltration process was carried out at a temperature of 175 °C for 1 hour.
